explanation: Ethene decolourises a reddish-orange bromine solution almost instantly as the halogen adds across its double bond — the standard laboratory test used to tell an unsaturated hydrocarbon from a saturated one, since alkanes don't react with bromine water under the same mild conditions.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: A reddish-orange bromine solution, with ethene gas passed through.
beaker_view.final_appearance: Colourless, once the addition is complete.
beaker_view.observation: The moment ethene gas passes into the solution, its reddish-orange colour fades to colourless — a quick, unmistakable sign of a carbon-carbon double bond reacting.
